function: Joint spectrum sub-band allocation and UAV flying-direction control by multi-agent deep active inference, with learned user rate-demand prediction, in a spectrum sharing UAV network (p. 7, 11).
system: Two cognitive UAVs at 100 m, 2 SUs, 3 PUs, 3 sub-bands of 20 MHz; LoS air-to-ground links; antennas, carrier frequency not stated; no RIS (p. 9, 12, 14).
method: Partially observable multi-agent deep active inference (value, policy, transformation networks), reinforcement-style with replay and TD-error updates, decentralized; ConvLSTM-attention demand predictor trained supervised offline with MSE (p. 4-8).
data_channel: Custom simulator: LoS air-to-ground inverse-square gain, ground links with path loss and Rayleigh fading; demand from public Milan telecom dataset (SMS, call, Internet), 3:1 split (p. 9, 12).
test_conditions: Allocation agents train and test in the same simulated network; separate convergence runs for overlapping PU/SU locations and a multi-cell ground network; demand data 3:1 train/test split (p. 12-15).
baselines: Non-learned: random scheme [32]. Learned: MAPPO [40], MA2C-DDPG [41], Q learning [28]; for demand prediction ConvLSTM [39] and ResNet [38] (p. 12-13).
metrics: Sum transmission rate of secondary network, average reward, convergence episodes, PU sum rate, per-service SU rates; demand prediction RMSE, MAE, R2 (p. 12-15).
complexity: Space-complexity formula; Table V: 3,845 parameters and 2.8 ms per iteration for the proposed scheme; Table IV: demand predictor 218,699 parameters, 116.4 ms forward pass (p. 14-15).
openness: none (no code or data released; the public Milan traffic dataset [34] is only cited as demand data, p. 12).
q1_support: p. 9: "between the UAV and the ground users is dominated by the line of sight (LoS) link"; custom LoS and Rayleigh model, with no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 13: "we conduct a convergence comparison in the scenario where there is an overlap between PU and SU locations"; a training-convergence curve, not a trained model tested in a new scenario.
q3_support: p. 13: "namely MAPPO [40], MA2C-DDPG [41], Q learning [28], and Random based scheme [32]"; p. 15: "obtains the highest sum transmission rate of the secondary system among all the considered benchmark schemes".
q4_support: p. 15: "schemes in terms of the number of parameters and computation time required for the forward propagation"; Table V lists parameters and ms per iteration, with a space-complexity formula.
q5_support: p. 12: "This dataset is authoritative and capable of capturing the key characteristics of 6G user demands"; a public traffic-demand dataset, not channels or signals. The channel is custom (p. 9) and no code link is given.
notes: Included, area 6, under the aerial-link rule: learned sub-band allocation (resource allocation on UAV links) is learned jointly with UAV trajectory (p. 11), and transmit power is fixed (Table III, p. 12). The ConvLSTM demand predictor is traffic prediction, a supporting module. The Milan dataset [34] is public but holds traffic demand, not channels, so q1 and q5 are 0 and the reviewer may confirm. Number of C-UAVs read from Fig. 14 (p. 14); Tables III to V read from page images.
